# Return-contract clarification decision criteria

Frozen before new model outputs. Use the exact existing 22-line candidate,
the completed development evidence and two fresh transfer pairs: current versus
absent, then candidate versus its own absent baseline. Each arm has three serial
attempts. Historical and retrospective observations remain outside this population.

| Decision | Predeclared condition |
| --- | --- |
| Adopt | Both campaigns complete with twelve measured outcomes and verified evidence, usage, reports and cleanup. All three candidate transfer submissions pass the reference and detect enabled-integer, enabled-zero, quantity-offset, quantity-below and quantity-above. They preserve permitted numeric type variation. Candidate correctness and coverage show no regression against current, interpreted through each pair's absent baseline. No material reliability, security or efficiency regression is observed. Existing development improvement and tagged-source justification support this narrow clarification. A passing transfer tie is sufficient. |
| Reject | Executable evidence shows a material candidate regression: incorrect reference behavior, lost defect/boundary coverage, overrestriction of permitted numeric types, or a material reliability, security or efficiency problem. Development success does not excuse transfer regression. |
| Defer | Operational stop, unsupported/unavailable evidence, inconsistent results, materially different absent baselines or other uncertainty prevents a defensible decision. Preserve measured failures and unavailable outcomes separately. Do not add attempts, replace trials or revise the grader or criteria. |

Primary success is reference correctness AND detection of all five declared
defects. Record every defect, reference result, submission hash, skill access,
native execution, usage and elapsed time. A failed reference earns no defect
credit. Inspect retained submissions as supporting evidence for executable grades.
Skill access alone does not establish instruction following.

The reference exercises Int32 and Int64 Quantity values. The public contract
permits other numeric implementations; requiring a concrete type beyond that
contract is overrestriction. Reference success verifies the exercised variation,
not every numeric implementation. Inspect submissions for extra type restrictions
and report unexercised generality without changing the frozen grader.

Report candidate/current successes and per-defect coverage alongside their own
absent baselines, including both present-minus-absent differences. Do not pool
the absent arms. If candidate is worse, or baselines differ enough to change the
interpretation, unexplained inconsistency defers adoption. This indirect
comparison cannot establish statistical non-inferiority or broad effectiveness
from three repetitions. A passing conclusion may be no regression observed on
these cases. Transfer is output-informed, not an untouched holdout.

A legitimate measured task failure may continue. Before dispatch two, dispatch
one must have six measured outcomes, essential submissions/grades/native
observations, known usage, verified reporting and completed cleanup. Any
operational failure, missing essential evidence, unknown usage or failed cleanup
stops the sequence. No retries, replacements, judges or continuation after a stop.

Efficiency is exploratory: compare token estimates and elapsed times against each
matched absent arm and across present arms. A threshold stop or unexplained
material cost/latency increase prevents adoption; small-sample variation alone
does not establish an efficiency regression or benefit. Retain the $5 per-pair
estimated-usage scheduling threshold and $3 reserve within an $8 planning
allocation ($16 total). These are not provider billing caps; CI is separate.

This file grants no model credentials, allocation claim, inference, live dispatch
or protected-environment approval. Final evidence publication stays separate from
the qualified execution revision. The historical PLAN criteria remain historical;
this decision table governs only these two new transfer campaigns.
